title: What borrowing really costs
blurb: Ravi needs money now and must pay it back later. Find out what that really costs him.
t1.title: Money now, money back later
t1.b1: Ravi needs {got1} for a phone. He has no savings, so he borrows it and promises to pay back {back1}.
t1.b2: To **borrow** is to get money now and repay it later. The extra you repay is the **cost of the loan**.
t1.b3: Think of renting a bicycle. You use it for a day and pay a fee. A loan is renting money, and the fee is interest.
q1.prompt: Meena borrows {got2} and repays {back2} in total. How much extra did she pay? Type a number in rupees.
q1.hint: Subtract what she received from what she repaid.
q1.explain: {back2} minus {got2} is {cost2}. That extra is the cost of her loan.
q2.prompt: Ravi gets {got1} and repays {back1}. What is the cost of his loan?
q2.hint: Cost of the loan = total repaid minus amount received.
q2.explain: He repays {cost1} more than he got. That is the cost of the loan.
t2.title: Cost as a percentage
t2.b1: **Interest** is the fee for using someone else's money. We often show the cost as a share of the amount borrowed, so loans of different sizes can be compared.
t2.b2.3: Cost as a share of the loan = {cost1} ÷ {got1} = {pct1}.
q3.prompt: Meena received {got2} and repays {back2}. The cost is {cost2}. What percentage of the loan is that? Type a percentage.
q3.hint: Divide the cost by the amount she received, then write it as a percentage.
q4.prompt: Two people each repay ₹1,000 more than they borrowed. One borrowed ₹5,000, the other ₹20,000. Who paid the higher cost, as a share of the loan?
q4.hint: Same rupees extra, but on a different starting amount.
q4.explain: The smaller loan costs a bigger share. ₹1,000 on ₹5,000 is 20%, but on ₹20,000 it is only 5%.
t3.title: Lab: what makes a loan cost more
t3.b1.prompt: Open the lab. Move the sliders for the amount, the yearly interest rate and the months. Watch the cost of the loan change.
q5.prompt: In the lab, set the amount to {labAmt}, the rate to {labRate} and the months to {labMonths}. What is the cost of the loan? Type a number in rupees.
q5.hint: Read the red "Cost of the loan" number in the lab.
q6.prompt: Keep the amount and the months the same. What happens to the cost of the loan if the interest rate goes up?
q6.hint: Drag the rate slider and watch the red number.
q6.explain: A higher rate means more interest each month, so the cost of the loan goes up.
t4.title: Borrowing from a friend
t4.b1: A friend may charge no interest. But a loan can cost in other ways: a strained friendship, a favour owed, or worry if you repay late. Money is not the only cost.
t4.b2: Many people think a loan with no interest is free. The rupees may match, but you still carry a promise. Be clear on the date and the amount.
q7.prompt: Asha borrows {fAmt} from a friend and repays exactly {fAmt}. Which statement is best?
q7.hint: Think about costs that are not rupees.
q7.explain: Her rupee cost is zero, but a late repayment could still hurt the friendship. Set a clear date.
q7.opt.a: It is completely free, so there is nothing to think about.
q7.fb.a: A friend loan has no interest, but it still carries a promise and the risk of a strained friendship.
q7.opt.b: No interest, but it still has a cost if she repays late.
q7.opt.c: It must be the most expensive kind of loan.
q8.prompt: A lender gives {fAmt} and wants {lBack} back. What is the cost of the loan in rupees? Type a number.
t5.title: Compare two offers
t5.b1: To compare loans, look at the **total you repay**, not just the monthly payment or a friendly-sounding rate. A lender should tell you the full cost in writing.
q9.prompt: Both lenders give {oGot}. Lender A wants {oA} back in total. Lender B wants {oB}. How many rupees cheaper is B? Type a number.
q9.hint: Subtract the smaller total repaid from the bigger one.
q9.explain: {oA} minus {oB} is {offerGap}. B costs that much less.
q10.prompt: Which is the best way to say what a loan costs?
q10.hint: Think about the two numbers you compare.
q10.explain: The cost of a loan is the total repaid minus the amount received.
q10.opt.a: The interest rate shown in big letters
q10.fb.a: A headline rate is only part of the story. Borrowed money is never free, so check the rupees you repay.
q10.opt.b: The size of one monthly payment
q10.opt.c: Total repaid minus the amount received
glossary.borrow_principal.def: The amount of money you actually receive when you borrow.
glossary.borrow_interest.def: The fee you pay a lender for using their money.
glossary.borrow_cost_of_loan.def: Total you repay minus the amount you received.
